title: fix(app-shell,plugin-designer): keep the required `*` out of three more forms' accessible names
body:
Fixes #10367

Clause-②: no

Dispatched by the `domain:ui#4` PM seat for objectui#10367; implemented in session `https://claude.ai/code/session_01BP8CMtACxTdLjqR6rhd33C`.

**File surface, amended twice.** The PR is three rounds, one commit per patch round.

- **Round 0** (`663fb5b2f`, `b48e7ae92`, `963d288c0`): the three sites the card names.
- **Round 1** (`2f3d01273`): adds `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/widgets.tsx`. The seat answered A to the report's open question and amended the claim in comment 5825438356 on objectui#10367. Without round 1, the PR would have hidden the `*` of the 11 registered `labelling: 'control'` widgets while they expose no required state.
- **Round 2** (`91c075fa4`): adds `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/color-variant-field.tsx`, through amendment 5825786390. It closes the same regression shape on `color-picker`, which round 1's report measured. Its `radiogroup` would otherwise have lost the `*` with no replacement.

Each patch round adds one pin case.

## What changed

Three forms drew the required `*` as a bare span inside the label that names the control, so assistive tech read it as part of the name ("Title *"), and no control reported that it was required. The fix at each site follows objectui#10361 (the console `FormPage`, landed `069ce12b`) and objectui#3299 (`ActionParamDialog`): the marker span gets `aria-hidden="true"`, and the control gets `aria-required`.

- **`packages/app-shell/src/views/ScreenView.tsx`** (flow screen fields). The `*` span inside `Label htmlFor=ff-NAME` is hidden. `ScreenFieldInput` puts `aria-required` on every control arm it renders (Input, Textarea, Checkbox, SelectTrigger) when the field is required. The attribute is omitted when the field is optional, so it is never written as "false".
- **`packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/SchemaForm.tsx`**.
  - Both `showRequiredStar` spans (the boolean row and the default row) are hidden.
  - So is the grid repeater's column-header `th` marker. Every cell control is named from that header through `aria-labelledby`, so its `*` reached every cell's name.
  - `FieldControl` takes a new internal `required` prop. `FieldRow` passes `showRequiredStar`, and a grid cell passes its column's `required`, so the state always matches the visible marker.
  - Every control `FieldControl` renders itself carries `aria-required` from that prop: both Select triggers, the Switch, the number and text Inputs, the long-string Textarea, the comma-separated list Input, and `RawJsonEditor`'s textarea.
  - `FieldControl`'s registered-widget branch passes the same prop to the widget (round 1), in a row and in a grid cell alike.
- **`packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/widgets.tsx`** (rounds 1 and 2).
  - `WidgetProps` gains an optional `required` member.
  - The file-local `controlNaming()` helper emits `aria-required` beside `id` / `aria-labelledby` when `required` is true, and omits it otherwise.
  - Ten of the eleven `labelling: 'control'` widgets pass `required` into `controlNaming()` at every call site they have. That covers the loading, failure and empty-catalog placeholder inputs, because they are the control on screen at that moment. The ten are `ref:object`, `ref:component`, `object-selector`, `field-selector`, `field-ref`, `view-ref`, `icon`, `color-input`, `string-tags` and `secret`.
  - None of the eleven spreads its naming props outside `controlNaming()`. `filter-builder` reaches the helper indirectly, through `FilterBuilderField`, and is the one deliberate exception (see below).
  - Round 2: `ColorSwatchGroupWidget` (the `color-picker` key, a `labelling: 'group'` widget) passes `required` to `ColorVariantPicker`.
  - Only an attribute is added. No widget's visual output or behaviour changes.
- **`packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/color-variant-field.tsx`** (round 2). `ColorVariantPicker` takes an optional `required` and puts `aria-required` on its `role="radiogroup"` element when it is true, omitting it otherwise. ARIA 1.2 supports the state on `radiogroup`. Its callers:
  - `ColorSwatchGroupWidget` (`widgets.tsx`): passes the field's flag.
  - `DashboardWidgetInspector`'s widget colour field: passes nothing, so it is unchanged.
  - `PageBlockInspector`'s `ColorPropField`: passes nothing, so it is unchanged.
  - `color-variant-field.labelling.test.tsx`, whose compile-time naming pins still hold, because an added optional prop changes no naming shape.
- **`packages/plugin-designer/src/AppCreationWizard.tsx`**. The App name and Title markers are hidden, and both inputs carry `aria-required="true"`. The separating space moved inside the hidden span. With the space outside it, Chromium 141 named the inputs `"App Name "` and `"Title "` (trailing space). With it inside, the names are exact. The rendered label looks the same.

Every marker also carries `data-required-marker="true"`. I chose it for consistency, not because it was required. It is the locator the shared form renderer's marker in `@object-ui/components` already carries, and objectui#10428 uses the same span shape. It gives the pins a locator that is not the a11y attribute under test. Each site keeps its existing visual classes.

Plus three pins beside the sources, and one changeset (`@object-ui/app-shell`, `@object-ui/plugin-designer`: patch). Rounds 1 and 2 extended the changeset body to state the widget half and the colour picker; its frontmatter is unchanged.

## Which surfaces may carry `aria-required` (why `filter-builder` does not)

`filter-builder`'s control is a popover trigger rendered as a plain `button`. ARIA 1.2 does not support `aria-required` on role `button`. I measured each surface shape with axe-core 4.13.0 (`aria-allowed-attr`) in headless Chromium 141, with `aria-required="true"` on it:

| surface | axe `aria-allowed-attr` |
|---|---|
| `button` (the `filter-builder` trigger) | **violation**: "ARIA attribute is not allowed: aria-required" |
| `button` with `role="combobox"` (`icon`, `object-selector`, `field-ref`, `view-ref`) | pass |
| `input type=text` (`string-tags`, and the `ref:*` / `field-selector` inputs) | pass |
| `input type=password` (`secret`) | pass |
| `input type=color` (`color-input`) | pass |
| `div role="radiogroup"` (`color-picker`, round 2; the real rendered SchemaForm DOM, not a synthetic shape) | pass, 0 violations on the page |

So `FilterBuilderField` keeps calling `controlNaming({ id, ariaLabelledBy })` without `required`, and a comment at that call site says why. Giving the trigger a role that supports the state would change its semantics, which is outside the "attributes only" scope.

## A1 — submit behaviour, per site (why `aria-required` everywhere, never native `required`)

| site | form element / `noValidate` | would native `required` change behaviour? |
|---|---|---|
| `ScreenView` | no form element in `ScreenView` or either host (`FlowRunner` wraps it in a Dialog with a button-driven `submit`; `ScreenPreview` in a card) | Yes, for the checkbox. `FlowRunner`'s required check counts an unchecked `false` as an answer, while native `required` on a checkbox means "must be checked". Any host form element would also add a browser verdict beside the runner's own check. |
| `SchemaForm`, its widgets and `ColorVariantPicker` | no form element in any in-repo host; `SchemaForm` is exported from the package root | Inside a host form element, the browser would block submit on its own verdict, beside the form's own validation. A `radiogroup` of buttons has no native `required` at all. |
| `AppCreationWizard` | no form element; the wizard gates Next and Create itself (`step1Valid` / `canProceed`) | Same: a host form element would gain a second, browser-side verdict. The component is exported and registered. |

No validation logic changed.

## Measured on main before the change (BASE `9ec8ceba0`)

The three new pin files (round-0 cases), run against the three source files checked out at BASE (armed trap, restore proven by blob hash == HEAD and empty `git diff HEAD`): **`Tests 6 failed | 3 passed (9)`**. The six required cases failed, and the three optional-field controls passed. Accessible names reported by testing-library on main: `App Name *`, `Title *` (wizard, ScreenView, SchemaForm), `Note *`, `Agree *`, `Kind *`, `Enabled *`, and the grid cell `Field *`. No control carried `aria-required`.

## The pins

- `packages/app-shell/src/views/ScreenView.requiredMarker-10367.test.tsx`
  - The card's probe: `getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Title' })` finds the required text field, which is `toBeRequired()` through `aria-required` and has no native `required`.
  - The marker is still drawn and is `aria-hidden`.
  - The Textarea, Checkbox and Select arms are found by their bare names and carry `aria-required`.
  - Control: optional fields have no marker and no `aria-required`.
- `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/SchemaForm.requiredMarker-10367.test.tsx`
  - The card's probe: a required string property's textbox has the computed name exactly `Title` and is `aria-required`.
  - The boolean row's required switch (no default) has the same shape.
  - A grid cell under a required column header is named `Field` and is `aria-required`. The optional column beside it is the in-render control.
  - **Round 1:** a required `string-tags` row is found as textbox `Tags`, and a required `icon` row as combobox `Glyph`. Both are named without `*` and carry `aria-required="true"`. An optional `string-tags` row in the same render (`Extra`) carries none. A grid cell whose required column renders `string-tags` is named `Tags` and carries `aria-required="true"`.
  - **Round 2:** a required `color-picker` field (schema palette `enum: ['red', 'blue']`) is a radiogroup named exactly `Accent` with `aria-required="true"`. An optional `color-picker` beside it (`Tint`) carries none.
  - Control: an optional string property has no marker and no `aria-required`.
- `packages/plugin-designer/src/AppCreationWizard.requiredMarker-10367.test.tsx`
  - The card's probe: `getByRole('textbox', { name: 'App Name' })` and `{ name: 'Title' }` both find their inputs, which are `aria-required` and have no native `required`.
  - Both markers are hidden.
  - Control: the optional Description textbox has no `aria-required`.

The markers are located by `data-required-marker`, never by `aria-hidden` itself.

**Every registered widget that can carry the state, measured (throwaway probes, not committed).** Each widget was rendered as a required and as an optional field, and I read its surface:

| widget | surface | required | optional |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ref:object`, `ref:component`, `field-selector` | `input` | `aria-required="true"` | absent |
| `string-tags` | `input type=text` | `aria-required="true"` | absent |
| `secret` | `input type=password` | `aria-required="true"` | absent |
| `color-input` | `input type=color` | `aria-required="true"` | absent |
| `object-selector`, `field-ref`, `view-ref`, `icon` | `button role=combobox` | `aria-required="true"` | absent |
| `filter-builder` | `button` | absent (by design, above) | absent |
| `color-picker` (round 2) | `div role=radiogroup` | `aria-required="true"` | absent |

## A2 — reverse proof (each fix committed first; mutations via `ablation-replace.mjs`, restore proven each time)

- **`aria-hidden` removed** from the `ScreenView` marker, on `663fb5b2f` (anchor 1 → 0, blob `bf60e49c5a3d` → `95117bc41e00`): `ScreenView.requiredMarker-10367.test.tsx` **`Tests 2 failed | 1 passed (3)`**. `Unable to find an accessible element with the role "textbox" and name "Title"` (and `"Note"`). The control case stayed green. Restored: blob == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty.
- **`aria-required` removed** from `SchemaForm`'s string Input, on `663fb5b2f` (anchor 1 → 0, blob `593cc82da19e` → `574671beef1a`; on-disk `aria-required={ariaRequired}` count 7 → 6): `SchemaForm.requiredMarker-10367.test.tsx` **`Tests 2 failed | 2 passed (4)`**. The string-property case and the grid string cell both failed on `toHaveAttribute('aria-required', 'true')`, because they share that control. Restored: blob == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty.
- **Round 1: the `aria-required` emit removed from `controlNaming()`**, on `2f3d01273` (anchor `'aria-required': required ? true : undefined };` 1 → 0, blob `b9bfb1c8ab4f` → `7c3f51bebcab`, on-disk emit count 0): **`Tests 1 failed | 4 passed (5)`**. Only the registered-widget case failed, on `expect(tags).toHaveAttribute('aria-required', 'true')`, as predicted before the run. Restored: blob == HEAD (`b9bfb1c8ab4f`), `git diff HEAD` empty.
- **Round 2: the `aria-required` emit removed from `ColorVariantPicker`**, on `91c075fa4` (anchor `aria-required={required ? true : undefined}` 1 → 0 in `color-variant-field.tsx`, blob `72518440a3f5` → `b46ef83b3b28`, on-disk emit count 0): **`Tests 1 failed | 5 passed (6)`**. Only the `color-picker` case failed, on `toHaveAttribute('aria-required', 'true')`, as predicted before the run. Restored: blob == HEAD (`72518440a3f5`), `git diff HEAD` empty.
- Declared, not hidden: my first round-0 leg-1 attempt was refused by the tool before running anything. The replacement string was a substring of the anchor, so its count could not rise. The file was restored and the leg was re-run with a distinct replacement.

## Real browser (headless Chromium 141, `/opt/pw-browsers/chromium`)

The DOM these forms render was dumped from throwaway renders (not committed) and loaded into Chromium. These are the CDP accessibility-tree names.

| form | this branch | same markup with the markers' `aria-hidden` removed (the shape on main) |
|---|---|---|
| ScreenView | textbox `Title` (required=true), checkbox `Agree`, combobox `Kind` (required=true) | `Title *`, `Agree *`, `Kind *` |
| SchemaForm | textbox `Title` (required=true), switch `Enabled`, grid cell textbox `Field` (required=true) | `Title*`, `Enabled*`, `Field*` |
| AppCreationWizard | textbox `App Name` (required=true), textbox `Title` (required=true), `Description` / `Icon` (required=false) | `App Name *`, `Title *` |
| SchemaForm `color-picker` (round 2) | radiogroup `Accent` (required=true), radiogroup `Tint` (required=false) | not dumped |

The round-1 widget surfaces were checked in Chromium through axe (the surface table above), not through a name dump.

## A3 — existing tests

- I grepped for tests that assert these labels with a `*` in the name. The one hit is `ScreenPreview.test.tsx`: `expect(screen.getByText('*'))`. It still passes unchanged, because `getByText` does not filter `aria-hidden` and the marker is still drawn. No test was edited or deleted.
- No source-text anchor pin (`readFileSync`-style) quotes a changed line. `column-identity.ratchet.test.ts` reads both `SchemaForm.tsx` and `widgets.tsx`; it was re-run green on `91c075fa4` (`7 passed`).

## Gates

Round-2 gates all ran on head **`91c075fa4`**, after its only commit:

- **Closure build and type-check:** `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/app-shell^...' --concurrency=2` then `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`): `Tasks: 28 successful, 28 total` (all cache hits; no dependency of app-shell changed), then exit 0.
  - The test tsconfig includes `color-variant-field.labelling.test.tsx`, whose compile-time pins say an unnamed or doubly-named picker must not compile. They still hold.
  - Outside `widgets.tsx`, the metadata-admin `WidgetProps` is named only in app-shell's metadata-admin (`form-spec.ts`, `SchemaForm.tsx` and four tests). It is not re-exported from any package barrel.
  - The one non-test direct use of a widget, `ActionDefaultInspector`'s `IconPickerWidget`, passes no `required` and is unchanged.
- **Tests (`pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`):** 257 files (255 in app-shell, the plugin-designer pin, and `packages/types`' `phase2-schemas.test.ts`, which names `PageBlockInspector` in a comment), in three chunks: `94 passed (94) / 1082 tests`, `82 passed (82) / 878 tests`, `81 passed (81) / 971 tests`.
  - The set is the round-1 union (files naming `SchemaForm` / `ScreenView` / `FlowRunner` / `ScreenPreview`, a `SchemaForm` host, `widgets`, a `*Widget` component, `WidgetProps`, `controlNaming` or `WIDGETS`) plus every test naming `ColorVariantPicker`, `color-variant-field`, `ColorSwatchGroupWidget`, `DashboardWidgetInspector` or `PageBlockInspector`.
  - That includes `color-variant-field.test.tsx`, `color-variant-field.labelling.test.tsx`, `SchemaForm.widgetLabelling.test.tsx`, `SchemaForm.optionVisibleWhen.test.tsx` and `PageBlockInspector.i18n.test.tsx`.
- **Check scripts, each exit 0:**
  - `check-changeset-presence`: `8 source file(s) of 2 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)`.
  - `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-overwrite`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:control-bytes`.
  - `check:new-line-citations`: `0 new citation(s)`.
  - `check-governed-queue-guard --test`: NOT GOVERNED.
- **`check:changeset-claims`:** it flagged five pending changesets that name `SchemaForm.tsx` or `widgets.tsx` (6247, 5596, 5040, 7125, 8218). I read each paragraph, and none is falsified.
  - By symbol, no pending changeset names `ColorVariantPicker` or `color-variant-field`.
  - `ColorSwatchGroupWidget` appears only in 6247, whose option-filtering claims are untouched.
  - `WidgetProps` appears only in 5040, and `controlNaming` only in 9889. Both still hold.
- **Lint:** the per-rule warning counts are identical before and after round 2 on `color-variant-field.tsx` (0e/2w), `widgets.tsx` (0e/37w), `SchemaForm.tsx` (0e/16w) and the pin (0e/0w).
  - Round-0 lint on the other files is unchanged, because those files did not move.
  - The population and invariance reasoning is as in round 0: the root `eslint.config.js` has no type-aware linting, and no rule in `eslint-rules/` reads the file system.
  - The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is left to CI.
- **Round-0 gates for files rounds 1 and 2 did not touch** (`ScreenView.tsx`, `AppCreationWizard.tsx` and their pins): measured on `963d288c0`.
  - `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-designer type-check`: exit 0.
  - The whole `packages/plugin-designer/`: `25 passed (25) / 182 tests`.
  - plugin-designer does not depend on app-shell, so rounds 1 and 2 cannot move either reading.

## Acceptance notes

- **`filter-builder`** is the one `labelling: 'control'` widget left without a required state, because its surface is a `button` (see above). The seat recorded this and did not fold it in.
- **Structured faces and the remaining `group` widgets** (composite, repeater, record, nested form, object rows; multiselect, condition and the like) render `role="group"`, which does not support `aria-required` in ARIA 1.2. Their hidden marker leaves no required channel there. `color-picker` is the one `group` widget whose surface (a `radiogroup`) supports it, and round 2 covers it.
- **Chromium's CDP tree reports no `required` for the checkbox (ScreenView) or the switch (SchemaForm)**, although both carry `aria-required="true"` in the DOM. objectui#10361 recorded the same reading for the `FormPage` checkbox.
- The master-detail widget's table header in `widgets.tsx` also draws a bare `*`. No cell there references that header by IDREF, so the `*` reaches no control's name. This is an observation, not this defect, and no round changes it.
